risks.ar: عدوى في الأنسجة العميقة قد تتطلب تصريفًا جراحيًا.

risks.en: Sciatic or other nerve injury from wrongly placed injections.
risks.ar: إصابة العصب الوركي أو أعصاب أخرى بسبب الحقن في موضع خاطئ.

risks.en: Oil embolism to the lungs causing coughing and breathlessness.
risks.ar: انسداد زيتي في الرئتين يسبب السعال وضيق التنفس.

long_term_en: Chronic blood-borne infections (HIV, hepatitis B/C) with lifelong consequences.
long_term_ar: عدوى مزمنة منقولة بالدم (فيروس نقص المناعة، التهاب الكبد B وC) ذات عواقب مدى الحياة.

myths.myth_en: Steroid users don't share needles, so infection isn't an issue.
myths.myth_ar: مستخدمو الستيرويدات لا يتشاركون الإبر، لذا العدوى ليست مشكلة.
myths.fact_en: Sharing of vials and equipment does occur, and non-sterile products cause infections even without sharing.
myths.fact_ar: تحدث مشاركة العبوات والأدوات فعلًا، والمنتجات غير المعقمة تسبب العدوى حتى دون مشاركة.

studies.title: The infectious complications of anabolic-androgenic steroid injection.
studies.finding_en: Literature review: infections attributed to steroid injection included HIV, hepatitis B and C, abscesses and a fungal eye infection; a quarter of adolescent users were estimated to share needles.
studies.finding_ar: مراجعة للأدبيات: شملت العدوى المنسوبة إلى حقن الستيرويدات فيروس نقص المناعة البشرية والتهاب الكبد B وC والخراجات وعدوى فطرية في العين، ويُقدَّر أن ربع المستخدمين المراهقين يتشاركون الإبر.

studies.title: Infectious disease, injection practices, and risky sexual behavior among anabolic steroid users.
studies.finding_en: Review: steroid users have been linked to HIV, hepatitis B and C and skin and soft-tissue infections; they engage in risky injection practices (less than people who inject drugs intravenously) and in more risky sexual behaviour than the general population.
studies.finding_ar: مراجعة: ارتبط مستخدمو الستيرويدات بفيروس نقص المناعة البشرية والتهاب الكبد B وC وعدوى الجلد والأنسجة الرخوة، ويمارسون حقنًا محفوفًا بالمخاطر (أقل من متعاطي المخدرات بالوريد) وسلوكًا جنسيًا خطرًا أكثر من عامة الناس.

studies.title: Counterfeiting in performance- and image-enhancing drugs.
studies.finding_en: UK study prompted by a series of muscle abscesses needing surgery: laboratory testing of underground-market products found about half of injectable steroids and a fifth of steroid tablets were counterfeit, and skin bacteria were cultured from samples.
studies.finding_ar: دراسة بريطانية دفعت إليها سلسلة من خراجات العضلات التي احتاجت إلى جراحة: وجد التحليل المخبري لمنتجات السوق السوداء أن نحو نصف الستيرويدات المحقونة وخُمس الأقراص مغشوشة، ونمت بكتيريا جلدية من بعض العينات.

studies.title: Impact of trenbolone on selected organs.
studies.finding_en: Review: trenbolone, never approved for human use, harms the nervous, reproductive and immune systems; most users report side effects, about a third get severe acne and gynaecomastia, and hypertension, arrhythmia, injection-site inflammation, nerve damage and tissue necrosis are also reported. Many effects remain unknown. (Injection-site harms here are reported for trenbolone but apply to injected steroids generally.)
studies.finding_ar: مراجعة: الترينبولون غير المعتمد للاستخدام البشري يضر الجهاز العصبي والتناسلي والمناعي؛ يبلّغ معظم المستخدمين عن آثار جانبية، ويصاب نحو الثلث بحب شباب شديد وتثدٍّ، كما سُجّل ارتفاع ضغط الدم واضطراب النظم والتهاب موضع الحقن وتلف الأعصاب وموت الأنسجة. وما زالت كثير من آثاره مجهولة. (أضرار موضع الحقن هنا مذكورة للترينبولون لكنها تنطبق على الستيرويدات المحقونة عمومًا.)

entries.en: Steroids and sudden death in athletes
entries.type_en: health topic: premature and sudden death
entries.type_ar: موضوع صحي: الوفاة المبكرة والمفاجئة
entries.summary_en: Autopsy series and national registries show that steroid users die earlier than non-users. Sudden deaths are often linked to enlarged, scarred hearts and early coronary disease, while suicides and violent deaths are also over-represented. Other drugs, diuretics and stimulants used alongside steroids add to the risk.
entries.summary_ar: تُظهر سلاسل التشريح والسجلات الوطنية أن مستخدمي الستيرويدات يموتون في سن أبكر من غير المستخدمين. وكثيرًا ما ترتبط الوفيات المفاجئة بقلوب متضخمة ومتليفة وأمراض شرايين تاجية مبكرة، كما تزيد نسبة حالات الانتحار والوفاة العنيفة. وتضيف المواد الأخرى ومدرات البول والمنشطات المستخدمة مع الستيرويدات إلى هذا الخطر.
entries.legal_status_en: Applies across illicit anabolic-androgenic steroid use; most compounds are prescription-only or controlled, and all are prohibited by WADA.
entries.legal_status_ar: ينطبق على الاستخدام غير الطبي للستيرويدات الابتنائية عمومًا؛ فمعظم المركبات لا تُصرف إلا بوصفة طبية أو خاضعة للرقابة، وجميعها محظورة من الوكالة العالمية لمكافحة المنشطات.

risks.en: Sudden cardiac death from arrhythmia in an enlarged or scarred heart.
risks.ar: الوفاة القلبية المفاجئة بسبب اضطراب النظم في قلب متضخم أو متليف.

risks.en: Heart attack from early coronary artery disease or clot.
risks.ar: النوبة القلبية بسبب مرض مبكر في الشرايين التاجية أو جلطة.

risks.en: Suicide, especially during withdrawal depression.
risks.ar: الانتحار، خاصةً أثناء اكتئاب الانسحاب.

long_term_en: Higher risk of premature death in registry studies of steroid users.
Lasting reduction in heart pumping function and earlier coronary artery disease, which may not fully recover after stopping.
long_term_ar: خطر أعلى للوفاة المبكرة في دراسات السجلات الخاصة بمستخدمي الستيرويدات.
انخفاض مستمر في كفاءة ضخ القلب وأمراض مبكرة في الشرايين التاجية، وقد لا يتعافى ذلك بالكامل بعد التوقف.

myths.myth_en: Bodybuilder deaths are just bad luck or genetics.
myths.myth_ar: وفيات لاعبي كمال الأجسام مجرد سوء حظ أو وراثة.
myths.fact_en: Population studies show consistently higher death rates among steroid users, and autopsies show steroid-type heart damage.
myths.fact_ar: تُظهر الدراسات السكانية معدلات وفاة أعلى باستمرار بين مستخدمي الستيرويدات، وتُظهر التشريحات تلفًا قلبيًا من النوع المرتبط بالستيرويدات.

studies.title: Sudden Cardiac Death in Anabolic-Androgenic Steroid Users: A Literature Review.
studies.finding_en: Review of 33 published sudden cardiac deaths in steroid users (almost all young men, most of them bodybuilders): nandrolone, testosterone and stanozolol were the steroids most often detected, and autopsies most often showed an enlarged heart and thickened left ventricle.
studies.finding_ar: مراجعة لـ33 حالة وفاة قلبية مفاجئة منشورة لدى مستخدمي الستيرويدات (معظمهم رجال شباب ولاعبو كمال أجسام): كان الناندرولون والتستوستيرون والستانوزولول أكثر الستيرويدات المكتشفة، وأظهر التشريح غالبًا تضخم القلب وزيادة سماكة البطين الأيسر.

studies.title: Sudden or unnatural deaths involving anabolic-androgenic steroids.
studies.finding_en: Forensic review of 24 deaths of steroid users in New South Wales (all men, average age early thirties): most were from drug toxicity, followed by suicide and homicide; nearly all had other drugs on board; nandrolone, stanozolol and methandienone metabolites were common, and autopsies showed testicular atrophy, left ventricular hypertrophy and coronary narrowing.
studies.finding_ar: مراجعة جنائية لـ24 حالة وفاة لمستخدمي ستيرويدات في نيو ساوث ويلز (جميعهم رجال في أوائل الثلاثينيات في المتوسط): كان معظمها بسبب التسمم الدوائي ثم الانتحار والقتل، ووُجدت مواد أخرى لدى جميعهم تقريبًا، وكانت نواتج الناندرولون والستانوزولول والميثانديينون شائعة، وأظهر التشريح ضمور الخصيتين وتضخم البطين الأيسر وتضيق الشرايين التاجية.

studies.title: Ventricular androgenic-anabolic steroid-related remodeling: an immunohistochemical study.
studies.finding_en: Autopsy study of two young bodybuilders who died after years of high-dose methenolone and nandrolone use and had no atherosclerosis or thrombosis: heart tissue showed cell death and scarring, and the authors attributed death to progressive steroid-related heart failure.
studies.finding_ar: دراسة تشريحية لاثنين من لاعبي كمال الأجسام الشباب توفيا بعد سنوات من استخدام الميثينولون والناندرولون بجرعات عالية دون تصلب شرايين أو جلطات: أظهر نسيج القلب موت الخلايا والتليف، وعزا الباحثون الوفاة إلى فشل قلبي تدريجي مرتبط بالستيرويدات.

studies.title: Cardiovascular Disease in Anabolic Androgenic Steroid Users.
studies.finding_en: Danish registry study of men sanctioned for steroid use in gyms, followed for about 11 years against matched controls from the general population: users had markedly higher rates of heart attack, coronary procedures, blood clots, arrhythmias, cardiomyopathy and heart failure.
studies.finding_ar: دراسة سجلات دنماركية لرجال عوقبوا لاستخدام الستيرويدات في صالات الرياضة، تابعتهم نحو 11 عامًا مقارنةً بمجموعة مماثلة من عامة السكان: كانت لدى المستخدمين معدلات أعلى بوضوح للنوبات القلبية وإجراءات الشرايين التاجية والجلطات واضطرابات النظم واعتلال عضلة القلب وفشل القلب.

studies.title: Anabolic-androgenic steroids among recreational athletes and cardiovascular risk.
studies.finding_en: Review focused on recreational athletes: steroid use brings high blood pressure, adverse lipids, faster atherosclerosis, subclinical cardiomyopathy and a higher risk of heart attack and sudden cardiac death; some structural heart changes persist after stopping.
studies.finding_ar: مراجعة تركز على الرياضيين الهواة: يجلب استخدام الستيرويدات ارتفاع ضغط الدم واضطراب الدهون وتسارع تصلب الشرايين واعتلالًا خفيًا في عضلة القلب وخطرًا أعلى للنوبة القلبية والموت القلبي المفاجئ، وتستمر بعض التغيرات البنيوية في القلب بعد التوقف.

studies.title: Cardiovascular effects of androgenic-anabolic steroids.
studies.finding_en: Review: steroid use has been associated with sudden cardiac death, heart attack, unfavourable blood lipids and cardiac hypertrophy; proposed mechanisms are atherosclerosis, clotting, blood-vessel spasm and direct injury to heart cells.
studies.finding_ar: مراجعة: ارتبط استخدام الستيرويدات بالموت القلبي المفاجئ والنوبة القلبية واضطراب دهون الدم وتضخم القلب، والآليات المقترحة هي تصلب الشرايين والتخثر وتشنج الأوعية والأذى المباشر لخلايا القلب.

entries.status_note_en: Not approved anywhere. It is in phase 3 trials for obesity and for fatty liver disease (MASH). Developed by Boehringer Ingelheim with Zealand Pharma.
entries.sport_status_en: Not specifically named on the WADA Prohibited List, but as a non-approved substance it falls under S0. Check the current list.
sci: Phase 2 human trials showed meaningful weight loss; phase 3 results are still coming
entries.summary_en: A weekly injected peptide that switches on both the GLP-1 and the glucagon receptors. Phase 2 trials showed meaningful weight loss and less liver fat. Phase 3 trials are running.
overview_en: Survodutide combines two signals. The GLP-1 part lowers appetite and slows the stomach, like semaglutide. The glucagon part is meant to raise energy use and help the liver burn fat.

Human trials so far are phase 2, where people lost a meaningful share of body weight and liver fat dropped. Larger phase 3 trials will show how it compares with approved drugs and how safe it is long term.
mechanism_en: Activates the GLP-1 receptor: less hunger and slower stomach emptying.
Activates the glucagon receptor: more energy use and more fat burning in the liver.
entries.evidence_en: Phase 2 randomised trials in people with obesity and in people with fatty liver disease. Phase 3 trials are under way.
side_effects_en: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and constipation were the most common side effects in trials, mostly early on.
A rise in heart rate has been seen with this drug class.
Long-term safety is not known yet.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.full_en: Glucagon / GLP-1 receptor dual agonist (IBI362, LY3305677)
entries.status_note_en: Approved in China in 2025 for chronic weight management. Not approved by the US FDA or in the EU. Developed by Innovent Biologics under licence from Eli Lilly.
entries.sport_status_en: Not specifically named on the WADA Prohibited List, but as a non-approved substance it falls under S0. Check the current list.
sci: Phase 3 trials in China showed clear weight loss; little data outside China
entries.summary_en: A weekly injected peptide that activates both the GLP-1 and glucagon receptors. Approved in China for weight management; not approved in the US or Europe.
overview_en: Mazdutide works on the same two receptors as survodutide: GLP-1 for appetite and glucagon for energy use and liver fat.
Large trials were run mainly in Chinese adults, where it caused clear weight loss compared with placebo. Data in other populations are limited.
mechanism_en: Activates the GLP-1 receptor: less hunger, slower stomach emptying, better blood sugar control.
Activates the glucagon receptor: more energy use and liver fat burning.
entries.evidence_en: Randomised phase 2 and phase 3 trials, mostly in China, for obesity and type 2 diabetes.
side_effects_en: Stomach side effects (nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting) were the most common in trials.
A rise in heart rate has been seen with this drug class.
Long-term safety outside trials is still being collected.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.status_note_en: Not approved. In phase 2 trials, mainly for fatty liver disease (MASH) and obesity. Developed by Altimmune.
entries.sport_status_en: Not specifically named on the WADA Prohibited List, but as a non-approved substance it falls under S0. Check the current list.
sci: Phase 2 human trials only
entries.summary_en: A weekly injected GLP-1 and glucagon dual agonist being tested mainly for fatty liver disease. Phase 2 trials showed weight loss and less liver fat.
overview_en: Pemvidutide is another dual GLP-1 and glucagon agonist. Its developer is focusing on the liver: reducing liver fat and inflammation in fatty liver disease.
Evidence so far comes from phase 2 trials. It is not approved anywhere.
mechanism_en: GLP-1 receptor: lowers appetite.
Glucagon receptor: pushes the liver to burn stored fat.
entries.evidence_en: Phase 1 and phase 2 randomised trials in people with obesity or fatty liver disease.
side_effects_en: Nausea and vomiting were the most common side effects in trials.
Long-term safety is not known.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.full_en: Unimolecular GLP-1 and amylin receptor agonist
entries.ar: أميكريتين · منبّه GLP-1 والأميلين في جزيء واحد
entries.status_note_en: Not approved. Tested in early human trials as a weekly injection and as a daily tablet. Novo Nordisk is moving it into larger trials.
entries.sport_status_en: Not specifically named on the WADA Prohibited List, but as a non-approved substance it falls under S0. Check the current list.
sci: Early human trials only, with promising weight loss
entries.summary_en: One molecule that acts on both the GLP-1 and the amylin receptors. Early human trials showed large weight loss, but the trials were small and short.
overview_en: Amylin is a hormone released with insulin that helps you feel full. Amycretin combines an amylin signal and a GLP-1 signal in a single molecule.
Early trials, as an injection and as a tablet, showed substantial weight loss over a few months. Larger and longer trials are needed before anyone knows how safe and effective it is.
mechanism_en: GLP-1 receptor: lowers appetite and slows the stomach.
Amylin receptor: adds a fullness signal from the brain.
entries.evidence_en: Phase 1 and phase 1b/2 human trials, small and short.
side_effects_en: Stomach side effects such as nausea and vomiting were common in early trials.
Safety over months and years is unknown.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.status_note_en: Approved by the US FDA in 2005 as an add-on for people with type 1 or type 2 diabetes who use mealtime insulin. It is not approved for weight loss.
entries.sport_status_en: Not named on the WADA Prohibited List; athletes should check the current list.
sci: Approved for diabetes; modest weight loss seen in trials
entries.summary_en: A man-made version of amylin, a fullness hormone released with insulin. Approved for diabetes in people who use insulin; it causes modest weight loss.
overview_en: Pramlintide was the first amylin-based drug. It slows the stomach, lowers the sugar spike after meals and helps people feel full.
Because it is used with insulin, the main danger is low blood sugar. It has to be managed by a doctor together with the insulin plan.
mechanism_en: Copies amylin: slows stomach emptying.
Lowers the release of glucagon after meals.
Adds a fullness signal in the brain.
entries.evidence_en: Randomised trials in type 1 and type 2 diabetes led to its approval. Weight loss was a secondary finding.
side_effects_en: Serious low blood sugar when combined with insulin, which is why it carries a strong warning.
Nausea, especially at the start.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.status_note_en: Approved by the US FDA in 2005 for type 2 diabetes, as the first GLP-1 drug. It is not approved for weight loss.
entries.sport_status_en: Not on the WADA Prohibited List.
sci: Many randomised trials in type 2 diabetes
entries.summary_en: The first GLP-1 drug, first found in the saliva of the Gila monster lizard. Approved for type 2 diabetes; weight loss is modest compared with newer drugs.
overview_en: Exenatide is a copy of exendin-4, a peptide found in Gila monster saliva that acts like the human gut hormone GLP-1 but lasts longer.
It opened the door to the GLP-1 drugs used today. Newer drugs such as semaglutide and tirzepatide cause much more weight loss.
goals_en: Blood sugar control in type 2 diabetes
mechanism_en: Activates the GLP-1 receptor: more insulin when blood sugar is high, less glucagon, slower stomach, less hunger.
entries.evidence_en: Many randomised trials in type 2 diabetes, including a large heart safety trial.
side_effects_en: Nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea.
Injection-site lumps with the long-acting form.
Rare pancreatitis has been reported with GLP-1 drugs.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.status_note_en: Approved by the US FDA in 2014 for type 2 diabetes, and later to lower the risk of heart attack and stroke in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is not approved for weight loss. Developed by Eli Lilly.
entries.sport_status_en: Not on the WADA Prohibited List.
sci: Large trials in type 2 diabetes, including a heart outcomes trial
entries.summary_en: A once-weekly GLP-1 drug for type 2 diabetes that also lowered heart events in a large trial. Weight loss is modest.
overview_en: Dulaglutide is a GLP-1 agonist attached to a large protein so it lasts a week.

A large outcomes trial in people with type 2 diabetes showed fewer heart attacks and strokes. It is a diabetes medicine first; weight loss is a side benefit and smaller than with semaglutide or tirzepatide.
goals_en: Blood sugar control in type 2 diabetes
mechanism_en: Activates the GLP-1 receptor: more insulin when sugar is high, less glucagon, slower stomach, less hunger.
entries.evidence_en: Many randomised trials in type 2 diabetes, including a large cardiovascular outcomes trial.
side_effects_en: Nausea, diarrhoea and vomiting.
Carries the GLP-1 class warning about a rare thyroid tumour type seen in rodents.
Rare pancreatitis has been reported.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.status_note_en: Approved by the US FDA in 2020 for obesity caused by certain rare genetic conditions (such as POMC, PCSK1 or LEPR deficiency), and later for Bardet-Biedl syndrome. It is not approved for common obesity.
entries.sport_status_en: Not named on the WADA Prohibited List; athletes should check the current list.
sci: Approved after trials in rare genetic obesity
entries.summary_en: A peptide that switches on the brain's main hunger brake (the MC4R receptor). Approved only for rare genetic forms of obesity confirmed by testing.
overview_en: In some rare genetic conditions the brain's satiety pathway is broken, and people feel hungry all the time. Setmelanotide acts after the broken step and restores the fullness signal.
It works in these specific conditions. It is not meant for common obesity, where GLP-1 drugs are used instead.
mechanism_en: Activates the melanocortin-4 receptor in the brain, which lowers hunger and raises energy use.
entries.evidence_en: Open-label phase 3 trials in people with confirmed rare genetic obesity.
side_effects_en: Darkening of the skin and moles.
Injection-site reactions and nausea.
Unwanted erections in men and sexual side effects.
Low mood and depression have been reported; the label warns about it.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.status_note_en: Not approved. Research is mainly in rodents and monkeys, where it caused weight loss along with signs of kidney strain.
entries.sport_status_en: Not specifically named on the WADA Prohibited List, but as a non-approved substance it falls under S0. Check the current list.
sci: Animal studies only, with kidney concerns
entries.summary_en: An experimental peptide designed to cut off the blood supply of fat tissue. It caused weight loss in obese monkeys, but also signs of kidney strain. No proper human trials have been published.
overview_en: Adipotide binds to a protein on the blood vessels that feed fat tissue and triggers those cells to die, so fat tissue shrinks.
In animal studies it caused weight loss, but kidney changes were seen. It is not a safe or tested option for people.
mechanism_en: Targets prohibitin on blood vessels that supply white fat, and triggers cell death there.
entries.evidence_en: Rodent and monkey studies. No published human efficacy trials.
side_effects_en: Kidney strain seen in animal studies.
Dehydration seen in animal studies.
Unregulated products: content and purity are not verified.
entries.storage_en: Lyophilised powder: fridge or freezer, away from light. After reconstitution keep it in the fridge and respect the period printed on the diluent vial.

entries.status_note_en: Not approved anywhere. It was studied in small human research studies on growth hormone release and the heart, but never developed into a medicine.
entries.sport_status_en: Prohibited at all times by WADA (S2: peptide hormones, growth factors and related substances). Check the current list.
sci: Small human research studies; no treatment trials
entries.summary_en: A six-amino-acid peptide that strongly triggers growth hormone release. It also raises cortisol and prolactin, and its effect fades with repeated use.
overview_en: Hexarelin is a stronger cousin of GHRP-6. It works on the ghrelin receptor in the brain and pituitary to release growth hormone.
Human studies showed big growth hormone pulses at first, but the response weakens over time. It has also been studied for heart effects in the lab.
mechanism_en: Activates the ghrelin (GHS-R1a) receptor, causing a growth hormone pulse.
Also binds CD36, a receptor studied for heart effects.
entries.evidence_en: Small human research studies on hormone release; animal heart studies.
side_effects_en: Raises cortisol and prolactin as well as growth hormone.
Hunger and water retention are reported.
Effect fades with repeated use.
Unregulated products: content and purity are not verified.
entries.storage_en: Lyophilised powder: fridge or freezer, away from light. After reconstitution keep it in the fridge and respect the period printed on the diluent vial.

entries.status_note_en: Not approved in the US or EU. In Japan it has been used as a diagnostic test for growth hormone deficiency.
entries.sport_status_en: Prohibited at all times by WADA (S2: peptide hormones, growth factors and related substances). Check the current list.
sci: Human research and diagnostic use; no treatment trials
entries.summary_en: A peptide that triggers growth hormone release through the ghrelin receptor. Used as a diagnostic test in Japan, not as a treatment.
overview_en: GHRP-2 is one of the growth hormone releasing peptides. It causes a strong growth hormone pulse and was used to test whether the pituitary can still make growth hormone.
There are no trials showing that it improves muscle, fat loss or recovery in healthy people.
mechanism_en: Activates the ghrelin (GHS-R1a) receptor in the brain and pituitary, causing a growth hormone pulse.
entries.evidence_en: Human endocrine research and diagnostic studies.
side_effects_en: More hunger.
Small rises in cortisol and prolactin.
Water retention and tingling hands are reported.
Unregulated products: content and purity are not verified.
entries.storage_en: Lyophilised powder: fridge or freezer, away from light. After reconstitution keep it in the fridge and respect the period printed on the diluent vial.

entries.status_note_en: Approved by the US FDA in 2017 only as a one-time oral test to diagnose growth hormone deficiency in adults. It is not a treatment.
entries.sport_status_en: Prohibited at all times by WADA (S2: peptide hormones, growth factors and related substances). Check the current list.
sci: Approved diagnostic test, backed by a comparison study
entries.summary_en: A drink taken once to test whether an adult's pituitary releases growth hormone. Approved as a diagnostic test only, not for treatment.
overview_en: Macimorelin is a peptide-like molecule that works by mouth. Doctors give it once and measure growth hormone in the blood afterwards.
It replaced harder tests for some patients. It is not used for muscle, fat loss or anti-aging.
mechanism_en: Activates the ghrelin receptor and triggers a growth hormone pulse that can be measured.
entries.evidence_en: A diagnostic study compared it with the standard insulin tolerance test.
side_effects_en: Taste changes, dizziness, headache and nausea after the test.
Some heart rhythm effects are listed on the label, so it is only given under medical care.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.ar: ميكاسيرمين · عامل النمو الشبيه بالإنسولين البشري
entries.status_note_en: Approved by the US FDA in 2005 for children with severe primary IGF-1 deficiency, a rare growth disorder. It is not approved for adults, muscle building or anti-aging.
entries.sport_status_en: Prohibited at all times by WADA (S2: peptide hormones, growth factors and related substances). Check the current list.
sci: Approved for a rare growth disorder in children
entries.summary_en: A lab-made copy of the body's own IGF-1. Approved only for a rare growth disorder in children. It is very different from the IGF-1 LR3 sold online.
overview_en: IGF-1 is the hormone that carries out most of growth hormone's growth effects. In a rare condition, children make growth hormone but not enough IGF-1.
For them, mecasermin helps growth. Outside that use, extra IGF-1 brings real risks, especially low blood sugar.
goals_en: Growth in children with severe primary IGF-1 deficiency (medical)
mechanism_en: Acts on the IGF-1 receptor in bone, muscle and other tissues, driving growth.
entries.evidence_en: Clinical studies in children with severe primary IGF-1 deficiency.
side_effects_en: Low blood sugar, which can be serious.
Enlarged tonsils, snoring and headaches.
Under a doctor it is monitored closely; outside medical care the risks are much higher.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.full_en: Blend of a GHRH analogue and a ghrelin receptor agonist
entries.ar: سي جي سي 1295 مع إيباموريلين · الخلطة الشائعة
entries.status_note_en: The blend has never been tested as a combination in a published trial. Each part was tested on its own in small early human studies, and neither is approved.
entries.sport_status_en: Prohibited at all times by WADA (S2: peptide hormones, growth factors and related substances). Check the current list.
sci: No trials of the combination; only separate early data
entries.summary_en: A popular blend of two growth hormone boosters sold together. The idea is that two signals give a bigger growth hormone pulse. The blend itself has no published human trials.
overview_en: CJC-1295 copies the brain's growth hormone releasing hormone. Ipamorelin acts on the ghrelin receptor. Each one triggers growth hormone in a different way, so the blend is claimed to work better together.
That claim comes from physiology, not from trials of the blend. What is sold varies a lot, and products are not regulated.
mechanism_en: CJC-1295: activates the GHRH receptor on the pituitary.
Ipamorelin: activates the ghrelin receptor, adding a second growth hormone signal.
entries.evidence_en: No trials of the blend. CJC-1295 and ipamorelin each have only small early human studies.
side_effects_en: Flushing, water retention, numb or tingling hands are reported.
Raised blood sugar is possible with higher growth hormone and IGF-1.
Unregulated products: content and purity are not verified.
entries.storage_en: Lyophilised powder: fridge or freezer, away from light. After reconstitution keep it in the fridge and respect the period printed on the diluent vial.

entries.ar: إم جي إف · عامل النمو الميكانيكي
entries.status_note_en: Not approved anywhere. Research is in cells and animals only; no published human trials.
entries.sport_status_en: Prohibited at all times by WADA (S2: mechano growth factors are named). Check the current list.
sci: Cell and animal studies only
entries.summary_en: A short piece of an IGF-1 variant that muscle makes after damage. Sold as a muscle repair peptide, but it has only been studied in cells and animals.
overview_en: After muscle is stretched or damaged, the IGF-1 gene can be spliced into a form called mechano growth factor. Lab studies suggest it helps activate muscle repair cells.
The synthetic peptides sold, often with PEG attached, are not the same as the natural protein, and there are no human trials.
mechanism_en: Thought to activate muscle stem cells (satellite cells) after damage.
routes_en: intramuscular or subcutaneous injection (no human studies)
entries.evidence_en: Cell and animal studies only.
side_effects_en: Safety in people is unknown.
Growth factors raise questions about tumour growth that have not been studied.
Unregulated products: content and purity are not verified.
entries.storage_en: Lyophilised powder: fridge or freezer, away from light. After reconstitution keep it in the fridge and respect the period printed on the diluent vial.

entries.status_note_en: Not approved. Eye-drop and topical forms have reached phase 2 and 3 trials (for example for dry eye and an eye surface disease). TB-500 is a short synthetic piece of it.
entries.sport_status_en: Prohibited by WADA: thymosin beta-4 and its derivatives such as TB-500 are named under S2.
sci: Some human trials of eye drops and topical forms; injected use not studied
entries.summary_en: The full natural peptide that TB-500 comes from. Eye-drop and skin forms have been tested in human trials for healing, with mixed results.
overview_en: Thymosin beta-4 is found in almost every cell. It helps cells move and build new blood vessels, which is why it was studied for wound and eye healing.
Human trials tested eye drops and gels, not injections. Injected use for sports injuries has not been studied in trials.
goals_en: Wound and eye surface healing (in trials)
mechanism_en: Binds actin inside cells, helping cells move to a wound.
Supports new blood vessel growth and lowers inflammation in lab studies.
entries.evidence_en: Phase 2 and 3 trials of eye drops; small trials of topical and intravenous forms; many animal studies.
side_effects_en: Eye drops were well tolerated in trials.
Injected use has unknown safety.
Growth-promoting effects raise theoretical cancer questions.
entries.storage_en: Lyophilised powder: fridge or freezer, away from light. After reconstitution keep it in the fridge and respect the period printed on the diluent vial.

entries.full_en: BPC-157-like peptide sold as an arginate salt
entries.status_note_en: Not approved anywhere. It is marketed as a more stable version of BPC-157. There is little or no peer-reviewed research on it, and its exact make-up varies between products.
entries.sport_status_en: Not specifically named on the WADA Prohibited List, but as a non-approved substance it falls under S0. Check the current list.
sci: Almost no published research
entries.summary_en: A newer peptide sold as a stable form of BPC-157. Claims rely on BPC-157's animal research; PDA itself has almost no published studies.
overview_en: PDA became popular after BPC-157 came under regulatory pressure in some countries. It is described as BPC-157 in an arginate salt form, said to be more stable.
Those claims have not been tested in published studies. Treat it as untested.
mechanism_en: Assumed to work like BPC-157; not studied directly.
entries.evidence_en: No published human trials and very little published research of any kind.
side_effects_en: Safety in people is unknown.
Unregulated products: content and purity are not verified.
entries.storage_en: Lyophilised powder: fridge or freezer, away from light. After reconstitution keep it in the fridge and respect the period printed on the diluent vial.

entries.full_en: Innate repair receptor agonist derived from erythropoietin
entries.status_note_en: Not approved. It has been tested in small phase 2 trials for nerve pain from small-fibre neuropathy (for example in sarcoidosis and diabetes).
entries.sport_status_en: Likely prohibited by WADA under S2, which covers innate repair receptor and other EPO-receptor agonists. Check the current list.
sci: Small phase 2 human trials with some positive signals
entries.summary_en: A small peptide made from part of erythropoietin (EPO). It is designed to calm inflammation and protect nerves without raising red blood cells.
overview_en: EPO is known for making red blood cells, but it also has tissue-protecting effects. ARA-290 keeps the protective part and drops the blood-boosting part.
Small trials in people with nerve damage reported less pain and some nerve fibre regrowth. Larger trials are needed.
mechanism_en: Activates the innate repair receptor (EPO receptor with CD131), which dampens inflammation and protects tissue.
entries.evidence_en: Small randomised phase 2 trials in small-fibre neuropathy; animal studies.
side_effects_en: Well tolerated in small trials.
Long-term safety is unknown.
entries.storage_en: Lyophilised powder: fridge or freezer, away from light. After reconstitution keep it in the fridge and respect the period printed on the diluent vial.

entries.full_en: Follistatin isoform (myostatin and activin binding protein)
entries.status_note_en: Not approved. Research is in animals and early gene-therapy studies for muscle diseases. The products sold for muscle growth have no human trials.
entries.sport_status_en: Prohibited at all times by WADA (S4: agents that block myostatin and activin, including follistatin). Check the current list.
sci: Animal and gene-therapy research only
entries.summary_en: A protein that blocks myostatin, the brake on muscle growth. Animals with more follistatin grow more muscle. There are no human trials of the injectable products.
overview_en: Myostatin limits how much muscle the body builds. Follistatin binds and blocks it, along with related signals called activins.
Gene-therapy research has looked at it for muscle-wasting diseases. Injectable follistatin bought for muscle is untested and may not even survive in the product.
mechanism_en: Binds myostatin and activin, removing their brake on muscle growth.
entries.evidence_en: Animal studies and small early gene-therapy studies in muscle diseases.
side_effects_en: Safety in people is unknown.
Activin also controls reproductive hormones; blocking it may affect fertility.
Unregulated products: content and purity are not verified.
entries.storage_en: Lyophilised powder: fridge or freezer, away from light. After reconstitution keep it in the fridge and respect the period printed on the diluent vial.

entries.status_note_en: Not approved anywhere, unlike plain Semax, which is approved in Russia. Claims of a stronger or longer effect are not backed by published human studies.
entries.sport_status_en: Not specifically named on the WADA Prohibited List, but as a non-approved substance it falls under S0. Check the current list.
sci: No published human studies
entries.summary_en: A chemically modified form of Semax, said to last longer. The modifications are real, but the claims about stronger effects have not been tested in people.
overview_en: Adding an acetyl group at one end and an amide at the other can protect a peptide from being broken down. That is the idea behind this version of Semax.
Plain Semax has Russian clinical use and studies. This modified version has none that are published.
mechanism_en: Assumed to act like Semax (raising BDNF and affecting dopamine and serotonin), with slower breakdown.
entries.evidence_en: No published human trials; claims extrapolate from Semax.
side_effects_en: Safety in people is unknown.
Nasal irritation and headaches are reported.
Unregulated products: content and purity are not verified.
entries.storage_en: Lyophilised powder: fridge or freezer, away from light. After reconstitution keep it in the fridge and respect the period printed on the diluent vial.

entries.full_en: P021, a peptide mimetic derived from ciliary neurotrophic factor
entries.ar: بي 21 · ببتيد مشتق من عامل CNTF
entries.status_note_en: Not approved. Studied only in cells and mice, including Alzheimer's disease models.
entries.sport_status_en: Not specifically named on the WADA Prohibited List, but as a non-approved substance it falls under S0. Check the current list.
sci: Mouse studies only
entries.summary_en: A small lab-made peptide based on a nerve growth factor called CNTF. In mice it boosted new nerve cell growth and memory. It has never been tested in people.
overview_en: P21 was designed to copy an active part of CNTF in a small molecule that can reach the brain.
Mouse studies looked promising for memory and brain ageing. Many brain drugs that work in mice fail in humans, so this is very early research.
mechanism_en: Raises BDNF and supports new nerve cell growth in the hippocampus in mice.
entries.evidence_en: Cell and mouse studies only.
side_effects_en: Safety in people is unknown.
Unregulated products: content and purity are not verified.
entries.storage_en: Lyophilised powder: fridge or freezer, away from light. After reconstitution keep it in the fridge and respect the period printed on the diluent vial.

entries.status_note_en: Sold as a medicine in Russia. Not approved in the US or EU. Human evidence comes from small Russian trials in mild cognitive problems.
entries.sport_status_en: Not named on the WADA Prohibited List; athletes should check the current list.
sci: Small, older Russian trials
entries.summary_en: A Russian nootropic built from two amino acids. Small Russian trials suggested benefits in mild cognitive problems; strong trials are missing.
overview_en: Noopept is a dipeptide-like molecule, not a classic peptide. It was developed in Russia as a memory drug.
The main trials were small and not done to modern standards. Effects in healthy people are not proven.
mechanism_en: Thought to raise BDNF and NGF in the brain and act on glutamate signalling; it breaks down into cycloprolylglycine.
entries.evidence_en: Small Russian clinical trials; animal studies.
side_effects_en: Headache, irritability and poor sleep are reported.
Products sold online are not regulated.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the product. Keep away from heat and direct sun.
entries.approved_elsewhere_en: Sold as a medicine in Russia

entries.full_en: Polypeptide extract from calf and pig brain cortex
entries.status_note_en: Approved in Russia and some post-Soviet countries for brain injury, stroke and cognitive problems. Not approved in the US or EU. Most studies come from Russia.
entries.sport_status_en: Not named on the WADA Prohibited List; athletes should check the current list.
sci: Mostly Russian studies of limited quality
entries.summary_en: A mix of small peptides extracted from animal brain tissue, used in Russia after stroke and brain injury. Evidence outside Russia is very limited.
overview_en: Cortexin is similar in idea to cerebrolysin: a brain-derived peptide mixture said to support nerve cells.
Because it is an extract, its exact contents are not a single defined molecule. Independent high-quality trials are lacking.
mechanism_en: Proposed to support nerve cell survival and balance brain signalling; not well defined.
entries.evidence_en: Mostly Russian clinical studies, small and of varied quality.
side_effects_en: Allergic reactions are possible with animal-derived extracts.
Imported products may not be regulated.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.status_note_en: Not approved anywhere. Research comes mainly from one Russian group, in cells, animals and small reports.
entries.sport_status_en: Not specifically named on the WADA Prohibited List, but as a non-approved substance it falls under S0. Check the current list.
sci: Cell and animal work from one research group
entries.summary_en: A three-amino-acid peptide from the same Russian group behind Epitalon. Claimed to protect the brain and slow ageing. Independent evidence is lacking.
overview_en: Pinealon belongs to the 'peptide bioregulators' idea: very short peptides said to switch on genes in specific organs.
Most work comes from the group that created it. Independent research and proper human trials are missing.
mechanism_en: Proposed to enter cells and influence gene activity; reduces oxidative stress in lab studies.
entries.evidence_en: Cell and animal studies, mostly from one research group.
side_effects_en: Safety in people is not well studied.
Unregulated products: content and purity are not verified.
entries.storage_en: Lyophilised powder: fridge or freezer, away from light. After reconstitution keep it in the fridge and respect the period printed on the diluent vial.

entries.status_note_en: Not approved. It failed to show benefit in a large trial in progressive supranuclear palsy, a brain disease, and is now studied in a rare genetic condition (ADNP syndrome).
entries.sport_status_en: Not specifically named on the WADA Prohibited List, but as a non-approved substance it falls under S0. Check the current list.
sci: A large human trial was negative
entries.summary_en: An eight-amino-acid brain peptide that looked protective in animals but did not help patients in a large trial. A good example of mouse results not carrying over.
overview_en: Davunetide comes from a protein that protects nerve cells. It stabilises the cell's internal skeleton (microtubules).
A large trial in a brain disease found no benefit. Research continues in a rare genetic condition where the parent protein is faulty.
mechanism_en: Stabilises microtubules inside nerve cells and interacts with tau protein.
entries.evidence_en: Phase 2 and a phase 2/3 trial; the larger trial was negative.
side_effects_en: Generally well tolerated in trials.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.status_note_en: A cosmetic ingredient, not a medicine. Evidence comes from small, mostly industry-funded cosmetic studies.
entries.sport_status_en: Not named on the WADA Prohibited List; athletes should check the current list.
sci: Small cosmetic studies
entries.summary_en: A skincare peptide that signals skin cells to make collagen. Small cosmetic studies reported fewer fine lines; strong independent trials are missing.
overview_en: Matrixyl is a piece of collagen with a fatty acid attached so it can enter the skin. In the lab it tells skin cells to make more collagen.
Results in people come from small studies, often by the makers. It is one of the better-studied cosmetic peptides, but the evidence is still modest.
mechanism_en: Acts as a 'matrikine': a collagen fragment that signals skin cells to build more collagen.
entries.evidence_en: Small cosmetic studies in people, plus lab studies.
side_effects_en: Usually well tolerated; skin irritation is possible.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the product. Keep away from heat and direct sun.

entries.status_note_en: A cosmetic ingredient, not a medicine. Evidence comes from small cosmetic studies.
entries.sport_status_en: Not named on the WADA Prohibited List; athletes should check the current list.
sci: Small cosmetic studies
entries.summary_en: A skincare peptide marketed as 'Botox in a bottle'. It is designed to relax expression lines, but the effect in studies is small and nothing like Botox.
overview_en: Argireline copies part of a protein that nerves need to release signals to muscle. In theory, less signal means less muscle pull and softer lines.
Small studies reported modest improvements. How much reaches the muscle through skin is unclear.
mechanism_en: Mimics part of the SNAP-25 protein and may reduce nerve signalling to small facial muscles.
entries.evidence_en: Small cosmetic studies and lab work.
side_effects_en: Usually well tolerated; skin irritation is possible.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the product. Keep away from heat and direct sun.

entries.status_note_en: Approved in the EU in 2014 and by the US FDA in 2019 to increase light tolerance in adults with erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP), a rare light-sensitivity disease. Given as an implant by trained doctors. Not approved for tanning.
entries.sport_status_en: Not named on the WADA Prohibited List; athletes should check the current list.
sci: Approved after randomised trials in a rare disease
entries.summary_en: The approved medical version of Melanotan I. An implant that darkens skin to protect people with a rare light-sensitivity disease. It is not a tanning product.
overview_en: Afamelanotide copies the hormone that tells skin to make melanin. For people with EPP, sunlight causes severe pain; more melanin lets them stay in light longer.
Melanotan products sold for tanning are not this regulated medicine and carry their own risks.
mechanism_en: Activates the melanocortin-1 receptor in skin, which increases melanin.
routes_en: implant under the skin (by a doctor)
entries.evidence_en: Randomised phase 3 trials in EPP.
side_effects_en: Nausea, headache and implant-site reactions.
Darkening of skin and moles; skin checks are advised.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.ar: إيه إتش كيه-كيو · ببتيد النحاس للشعر
entries.status_note_en: A cosmetic ingredient, not a medicine. Evidence for hair growth comes from lab studies on hair follicles; no solid human trials.
entries.sport_status_en: Not named on the WADA Prohibited List; athletes should check the current list.
sci: Lab studies only
entries.summary_en: A copper peptide related to GHK-Cu, sold for hair growth. Lab studies on hair follicles look interesting, but there are no proper human trials.
overview_en: AHK-Cu is a close relative of GHK-Cu. In lab studies it helped hair follicle cells survive longer.
Hair loss products with it are sold widely, but proof in people is missing. Proven treatments for hair loss exist and are worth discussing with a doctor first.
mechanism_en: In lab studies it supported hair follicle cells and blood vessel growth.
entries.evidence_en: Cell and hair follicle lab studies.
side_effects_en: Scalp irritation is possible.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the product. Keep away from heat and direct sun.

entries.ar: غونادوريلين · الهرمون المطلق لموجهات الغدد التناسلية
entries.status_note_en: Gonadorelin products were approved by the US FDA in the past for diagnostic testing and for a fertility pump; those branded products were later discontinued. Today it is mostly supplied by compounding pharmacies, which is a less controlled route.
entries.sport_status_en: Prohibited by WADA for males (S2: chorionic gonadotrophin, LH and their releasing factors). Check the current list.
sci: Long medical history in testing and fertility; little data for the uses it is sold for now
entries.summary_en: A lab-made copy of the brain hormone that tells the pituitary to release LH and FSH. Used in medicine for testing and fertility. Popular with men on testosterone, where evidence is thin.
overview_en: GnRH is released in pulses from the brain. Each pulse tells the pituitary to release LH and FSH, which drive the testes or ovaries.

Given in the right pulse pattern it can restore fertility in some people. Given continuously, it does the opposite and shuts the system down. Men on testosterone use it hoping to keep their testes active, but good trials for that use are lacking. Any use belongs with a doctor.
mechanism_en: Activates GnRH receptors on the pituitary, releasing LH and FSH.
entries.evidence_en: Decades of medical use in testing and fertility care; few trials for the uses it is now sold for.
side_effects_en: Headache, flushing and injection-site reactions.
The wrong pattern of use can suppress, not stimulate, hormones.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.ar: إتش سي جي · هرمون موجّه الغدد التناسلية المشيمائي
entries.status_note_en: Approved by the US FDA for fertility treatment in women, for hypogonadism caused by the pituitary in men, and for undescended testes in boys. Its label states it has not been shown to help weight loss.
entries.sport_status_en: Prohibited by WADA for males (S2: chorionic gonadotrophin, LH and their releasing factors). Check the current list.
sci: Long-established fertility medicine
entries.summary_en: The pregnancy hormone, used in medicine because it acts like LH. Approved for fertility and some hormone problems. It does not help weight loss.
overview_en: hCG is a protein hormone (larger than a typical peptide) made in pregnancy. It activates the same receptor as LH, so in men it tells the testes to make testosterone and in women it triggers ovulation.
It was once promoted for weight loss with very low calorie diets. Trials showed no benefit beyond the diet itself.
mechanism_en: Activates the LH receptor in the testes and ovaries.
entries.evidence_en: Decades of clinical use and trials in fertility care; trials of hCG for weight loss were negative.
side_effects_en: In women, ovarian hyperstimulation is a serious risk without monitoring.
In men, breast tenderness or growth can occur from raised estrogen.
Used outside medical care, the wrong amounts can disturb the hormone system.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.status_note_en: Not approved. Research is in cells and animals; human studies only measure the body's own levels.
entries.sport_status_en: Not specifically named on the WADA Prohibited List, but as a non-approved substance it falls under S0. Check the current list.
sci: Cell and animal data; human studies are observational
entries.summary_en: A small peptide made from mitochondrial DNA, a cousin of MOTS-c. In animals it protects cells under stress. It has not been tested as a treatment in people.
overview_en: Humanin was found in the brains of people who did not develop Alzheimer's-type damage in one area. Lab work showed it protects nerve and other cells.
Levels fall with age in many studies, and longer-lived families have been reported to have higher levels. None of this shows that taking it helps people.
mechanism_en: Released from mitochondria as a signal; protects cells from stress-related death in lab studies.
Improves insulin sensitivity in animal studies.
entries.evidence_en: Cell and animal studies; observational human studies of natural levels.
side_effects_en: Safety in people is unknown.
Unregulated products: content and purity are not verified.
entries.storage_en: Lyophilised powder: fridge or freezer, away from light. After reconstitution keep it in the fridge and respect the period printed on the diluent vial.

entries.ar: فوكسو 4 دي آر آي · ببتيد مزيل الخلايا الهرمة
entries.status_note_en: Not approved. Evidence comes from a small number of cell and mouse studies; no published human trials.
entries.sport_status_en: Not specifically named on the WADA Prohibited List, but as a non-approved substance it falls under S0. Check the current list.
sci: Mouse studies only
entries.summary_en: An experimental peptide that pushes old, 'senescent' cells to die. In aged mice it improved fur, fitness and kidney function. It has never been tested in people.
overview_en: Senescent cells stop dividing but stay in tissues, sending out inflammatory signals. Clearing them is a major idea in ageing research.
FOXO4-DRI breaks a link that keeps these cells alive. The mouse results were striking, but they have not been tested in humans, and killing cells carries real risks.
mechanism_en: Blocks the FOXO4 and p53 interaction in senescent cells, letting them self-destruct.
entries.evidence_en: Cell and mouse studies.
side_effects_en: Safety in people is unknown.
Unregulated products: content and purity are not verified.
entries.storage_en: Lyophilised powder: fridge or freezer, away from light. After reconstitution keep it in the fridge and respect the period printed on the diluent vial.

entries.full_en: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (a coenzyme, not a peptide)
entries.ar: إن إيه دي+ · مرافق الإنزيم للطاقة
entries.status_note_en: NAD+ is not an approved medicine for energy, ageing or recovery. Only small human studies of NAD+ injections and drips exist. Its oral building blocks, NMN and NR, have been tested in more human trials.
entries.sport_status_en: Not named on the WADA Prohibited List. Note that WADA limits intravenous infusions and injections above a set volume, whatever they contain. Check the current list.
sci: Small human studies of injections and drips; no good outcome trials
entries.summary_en: A coenzyme every cell needs to make energy in the mitochondria. Levels fall with age. NAD+ drips and shots are popular, but human evidence is thin.
overview_en: NAD+ is not a peptide; it sits in this library because it is used the same way, by injection or drip. It carries energy in the mitochondria and fuels repair enzymes such as sirtuins and PARPs.

NAD+ levels fall with age in animals and some human tissues. Raising them helped ageing mice in several ways. In people, small studies show injected NAD+ is quickly broken down; whether it brings real health benefits is unknown.
mechanism_en: Carries electrons in the mitochondria to help make ATP, the cell's energy.
Fuels sirtuin and PARP enzymes involved in DNA repair and metabolism.
entries.evidence_en: Small human pharmacology studies of infusions; larger body of trials for oral precursors (NMN, NR); strong animal research.
side_effects_en: Drips given fast commonly cause flushing, chest tightness, nausea and cramps.
Injection-site pain.
Drips outside medical settings carry infection and vein risks.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.ar: لارازوتايد · منظّم الوصلات المحكمة في الأمعاء
entries.status_note_en: Not approved. A phase 3 trial in coeliac disease was stopped in 2022 after an interim look suggested it was unlikely to succeed.
entries.sport_status_en: Not specifically named on the WADA Prohibited List, but as a non-approved substance it falls under S0. Check the current list.
sci: Mixed phase 2 results; phase 3 stopped
entries.summary_en: An oral peptide designed to tighten the gut lining in coeliac disease. Phase 2 trials were mixed and the phase 3 trial was stopped.
overview_en: Larazotide acts on the tight junctions between gut cells, aiming to stop gluten fragments from leaking through.
It is often mentioned in 'leaky gut' discussions, but the trial evidence did not hold up.
mechanism_en: Blocks zonulin-driven opening of tight junctions between gut cells.
entries.evidence_en: Phase 2 trials with mixed results; a phase 3 trial stopped early.
side_effects_en: Well tolerated in trials.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.status_note_en: Approved in some European countries in combination with phentolamine as an injection for erectile dysfunction. Not approved by the US FDA; it was tested for severe COVID-19 lung failure without approval.
entries.sport_status_en: Not named on the WADA Prohibited List; athletes should check the current list.
sci: Some human trials; mixed results
entries.summary_en: A copy of a natural gut and brain peptide that relaxes blood vessels and calms inflammation. Used in some countries for erectile dysfunction; other uses are unproven.
overview_en: VIP widens blood vessels, relaxes smooth muscle and dampens immune activity.
Nasal VIP is promoted in some clinics for mould-related illness and other conditions. Those uses have not been proven in solid trials.
mechanism_en: Activates VPAC receptors: blood vessels widen, smooth muscle relaxes, inflammation drops.
entries.evidence_en: Clinical trials in erectile dysfunction and in COVID-19 lung failure; small studies for other uses.
side_effects_en: Flushing, low blood pressure and fast heartbeat.
Diarrhoea with intravenous use.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.status_note_en: Approved by the US FDA in 1988 for acromegaly (too much growth hormone) and for symptoms of certain hormone-making tumours. Developed by Novartis.
entries.sport_status_en: Not named on the WADA Prohibited List; athletes should check the current list.
sci: Decades of approved medical use
entries.summary_en: A long-lasting copy of somatostatin, the body's 'off switch' for many hormones. Used for growth hormone excess and some tumours.
overview_en: Somatostatin lowers growth hormone, insulin, glucagon and gut hormones. Octreotide lasts much longer than the natural hormone.
It is a specialist medicine and a good reminder that peptides are a normal part of mainstream medicine.
mechanism_en: Activates somatostatin receptors, switching off growth hormone and several gut hormones.
entries.evidence_en: Decades of clinical trials and use.
side_effects_en: Stomach upset and gallstones with long-term use.
Changes in blood sugar.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.ar: ديسموبريسين · نظير الهرمون المضاد لإدرار البول
entries.status_note_en: Approved by the US FDA for central diabetes insipidus, bedwetting and some bleeding disorders.
entries.sport_status_en: Prohibited at all times by WADA (S5: diuretics and masking agents name desmopressin). Check the current list.
sci: Long-established approved medicine
entries.summary_en: A copy of the body's water-saving hormone. It helps the kidneys hold water. Used for diabetes insipidus, bedwetting and some bleeding disorders.
overview_en: Vasopressin tells the kidneys to keep water. Desmopressin does the same with fewer effects on blood pressure.
Because it holds water, drinking too much on it can dilute the blood dangerously.
mechanism_en: Activates V2 receptors in the kidney, so less water is lost in urine.
entries.evidence_en: Decades of clinical use and trials.
side_effects_en: Low sodium in the blood, which can cause confusion and seizures; doctors give fluid rules.
Headache.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.ar: تيريباراتايد · جزء هرمون الغدة الجار درقية
entries.status_note_en: Approved by the US FDA in 2002 for osteoporosis in people at high risk of fractures. Developed by Eli Lilly.
entries.sport_status_en: Not named on the WADA Prohibited List; athletes should check the current list.
sci: Large fracture trials
entries.summary_en: The active part of parathyroid hormone. Approved for osteoporosis: it builds new bone and lowers fracture risk.
overview_en: Most osteoporosis drugs slow bone loss. Teriparatide is different: given in daily pulses it tells the body to build new bone.
Large trials showed fewer spine fractures. Treatment time is limited and followed by another bone medicine.
mechanism_en: Short daily pulses of PTH activate bone-building cells more than bone-removing cells.
entries.evidence_en: Large randomised fracture trials.
side_effects_en: Dizziness and leg cramps.
Raised calcium.
Early rat studies found bone tumours at high exposure; this warning was later softened after human data.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.status_note_en: Approved by the US FDA in 2017 for osteoporosis in people at high risk of fractures.
entries.sport_status_en: Not named on the WADA Prohibited List; athletes should check the current list.
sci: Large fracture trial
entries.summary_en: A bone-building peptide similar to teriparatide. Approved for osteoporosis at high fracture risk.
overview_en: Abaloparatide copies a related hormone, PTHrP. Like teriparatide, daily pulses build new bone.
A large trial showed fewer spine and other fractures than placebo.
mechanism_en: Activates the PTH1 receptor in a way that favours bone building.
entries.evidence_en: Large randomised fracture trial.
side_effects_en: Dizziness, fast heartbeat and nausea.
Raised calcium.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.status_note_en: Approved by the US FDA in 2012 for irritable bowel syndrome with constipation and chronic constipation in adults. Not for young children.
entries.sport_status_en: Not named on the WADA Prohibited List; athletes should check the current list.
sci: Large randomised trials
entries.summary_en: A peptide taken by mouth that works inside the gut. Approved for constipation and IBS with constipation.
overview_en: Most peptides are broken down when swallowed. Linaclotide is built to work inside the gut without being absorbed.
It draws water into the bowel and eases gut pain signals.
mechanism_en: Activates guanylate cyclase-C in the gut lining: more fluid in the bowel, less pain signalling.
entries.evidence_en: Large randomised phase 3 trials.
side_effects_en: Diarrhoea, sometimes severe.
Dehydration risk, which is why it is not for young children.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.status_note_en: Approved by the US FDA in 2021 to increase growth in children with achondroplasia whose growth plates are still open.
entries.sport_status_en: Not named on the WADA Prohibited List; athletes should check the current list.
sci: Randomised trial in children with achondroplasia
entries.summary_en: A peptide that releases a brake on bone growth. Approved for children with achondroplasia, the most common form of short-limbed dwarfism.
overview_en: In achondroplasia, a gene change over-activates a brake on growth plates. Vosoritide counters that brake.
A randomised trial showed faster yearly growth. It only works while growth plates are open.
mechanism_en: Activates the NPR-B receptor, which counters the over-active FGFR3 signal in growth plates.
entries.evidence_en: Randomised phase 3 trial and extension studies.
side_effects_en: Injection-site reactions.
Short drops in blood pressure.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.status_note_en: Approved by the US FDA for advanced prostate cancer, endometriosis, uterine fibroids and early puberty in children.
entries.sport_status_en: Prohibited by WADA for males (S2: chorionic gonadotrophin, LH and their releasing factors). Check the current list.
sci: Decades of approved use
entries.summary_en: A GnRH copy that, given continuously, shuts down the sex hormone system. Used for prostate cancer, endometriosis and early puberty.
overview_en: The body releases GnRH in pulses. A steady signal makes the pituitary stop responding, so testosterone and estrogen fall.
This is the opposite of what pulsed gonadorelin does, which shows how much the pattern of a hormone matters.
mechanism_en: Continuous activation of the GnRH receptor desensitises the pituitary, lowering LH, FSH and sex hormones.
entries.evidence_en: Decades of clinical trials and use.
side_effects_en: Hot flushes, low libido and bone loss from low sex hormones.
A short hormone flare at the start.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.status_note_en: Approved by the US FDA in 2012 for short bowel syndrome in people who need IV nutrition.
entries.sport_status_en: Not named on the WADA Prohibited List; athletes should check the current list.
sci: Randomised trials in short bowel syndrome
entries.summary_en: A copy of the gut-growth hormone GLP-2. Approved for short bowel syndrome, where it helps the remaining bowel absorb more.
overview_en: After large parts of the bowel are removed, some people cannot absorb enough food. Teduglutide makes the remaining gut lining grow and absorb better.
Because it makes gut tissue grow, doctors check the bowel for growths before and during treatment.
mechanism_en: Activates GLP-2 receptors, increasing gut lining growth and absorption.
entries.evidence_en: Randomised trials in short bowel syndrome.
side_effects_en: Belly pain and swelling.
Risk of gut growths (polyps); colonoscopy checks are required.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.full_en: N-type calcium channel blocker from cone snail venom
entries.ar: زيكونوتايد · ببتيد من سم القواقع المخروطية
entries.status_note_en: Approved by the US FDA in 2004 for severe chronic pain, given through a pump into the spinal fluid when other treatments fail.
entries.sport_status_en: Not named on the WADA Prohibited List; athletes should check the current list.
sci: Approved after randomised trials
entries.summary_en: A painkiller copied from cone snail venom. Given only into the spinal fluid by a pump, for severe pain that nothing else controls.
overview_en: Ziconotide blocks a type of calcium channel that pain nerves use to pass signals. It is not an opioid.
It carries strong warnings for mental and nerve side effects, so it is used only by pain specialists.
mechanism_en: Blocks N-type calcium channels on pain nerves in the spinal cord.
entries.evidence_en: Randomised trials in severe chronic pain.
side_effects_en: Dizziness, confusion and memory problems.
Serious mood and psychiatric effects; the label carries a strong warning.
entries.storage_en: Follow the storage instructions on the pharmacy label.

entries.full_en: The main androgen, made in the testes, ovaries and adrenal glands
entries.summary_en: The main male sex hormone, also made in smaller amounts by women. In men with a confirmed deficiency, treatment under a doctor helps libido, mood, bone and blood count. Taken without need or above normal levels, it causes real harm.
does_en: Builds and keeps muscle and bone.
Drives libido and supports erections.
Supports sperm production (together with FSH).
Stimulates red blood cell production.
Affects mood, energy and fat distribution.
men_en: It is the main sex hormone. Most is made in the testes, under the control of LH from the pituitary.
Levels fall slowly with age. Low levels with symptoms (low libido, fatigue, low mood, weaker bones) is called hypogonadism.
A diagnosis needs symptoms plus repeated morning blood tests, because levels swing during the day.
Testosterone from outside switches off the body's own production, including sperm production.
women_en: Women make testosterone too, in much smaller amounts, in the ovaries and adrenal glands.
It supports libido, bone and muscle.
Some specialists prescribe testosterone for low sexual desire after menopause, at levels matched to normal female ranges.
Too much causes acne, unwanted hair growth, scalp hair loss and a deeper voice. Voice changes can be permanent.
Raised testosterone is part of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).
trials_en: In older men with confirmed low testosterone, large placebo-controlled trials showed modest gains in sexual function, mood, bone density and anaemia. Energy and memory did not clearly improve.

A large heart safety trial in men with low testosterone and high heart risk found treatment was not worse than placebo for heart attack and stroke. Some other problems, such as atrial fibrillation and blood clots in the lungs, were more common.
In women after menopause, trials support testosterone for low sexual desire when female-range levels are kept. Long-term safety data are limited.

myths.myth_en: Testosterone therapy causes heart attacks.
myths.fact_en: Early worrying studies were not confirmed. In a large trial of men with true low testosterone treated under care, heart attacks and strokes were not increased. Heart damage is tied to misuse at levels far above normal.

myths.myth_en: Testosterone therapy causes prostate cancer.
myths.fact_en: This old belief has not held up in modern studies of men treated within normal ranges. Doctors still check the prostate before and during treatment.

myths.myth_en: More testosterone is always better.
myths.fact_en: Benefits flatten out once levels are normal. Going above normal adds risk (thick blood, infertility, heart strain) without health benefit.

myths.myth_en: TRT and steroid use are the same thing.
myths.fact_en: TRT restores a missing hormone to normal with tests and follow-up. Misuse pushes levels far above normal, often with other drugs and no monitoring.

entries.care_en: TRT (testosterone replacement therapy) is for men with a confirmed deficiency. A doctor checks blood levels, red blood cell count and, where relevant, the prostate, before and during treatment, and adjusts it to stay in the normal range. Fertility is discussed first, because outside testosterone lowers sperm production. Steroid misuse is the opposite: levels pushed far above normal, often stacked with other drugs, bought without a prescription and with no tests.
entries.abuse_en: Being natural does not make any amount safe. Testosterone taken without a deficiency, or at levels above the normal range, shuts down the body's own hormone production, shrinks the testes, thickens the blood and strains the heart. Products bought outside pharmacies may also be fake or contaminated.
good_en: Better libido and sexual function in men with confirmed low levels.
Better bone density and correction of mild anaemia.
Improved mood in some men.
Some gain in muscle and loss of fat.
risks_en: Thick blood (high haematocrit) and clots when levels run too high without checks.
Lower sperm production and fertility, which a doctor plans for and unsupervised users often notice too late.
Acne, oily skin and breast tissue growth when levels or conversion to estrogen are off.
Heart strain and liver damage are linked to misuse at high levels, especially with oral steroids.

entries.summary_en: The main female sex hormone, also essential in men. In women around menopause, hormone therapy under a doctor relieves symptoms and protects bone. Problems come from the wrong type, wrong person or no monitoring.
does_en: Controls the menstrual cycle and prepares the uterus.
Protects bone strength in both sexes.
Keeps vaginal and urinary tissue healthy.
Affects cholesterol, skin, brain and mood.
In men, supports libido, erections and sperm.
men_en: Men make estradiol mainly by converting testosterone (through the aromatase enzyme), in fat, brain and bone.
It is needed for strong bones, libido, erections and healthy sperm.
Too high (often from excess testosterone or a lot of body fat) can cause breast tissue growth and water retention.
Too low, often from misusing aromatase-blocking drugs, causes joint pain, low libido, low mood and bone loss.
women_en: It is the main female sex hormone, made mostly by the ovaries until menopause.
Levels rise and fall across the cycle and drop at menopause.
Falling levels cause hot flushes, night sweats, poor sleep, vaginal dryness and faster bone loss.
Hormone therapy (HRT) replaces it. Women with a uterus also need progesterone or a progestogen to protect the uterine lining.
trials_en: A large US trial reported in 2002 found more breast cancer, strokes and clots with combined hormone therapy in women who were on average more than ten years past menopause. Prescriptions dropped worldwide.

Later analyses showed the risks depend on age, time since menopause, and the type of hormone. For healthy women under 60 or within about ten years of menopause, the benefits for symptoms and bone often outweigh the risks.
In the same trial, estrogen alone (in women without a uterus) did not raise breast cancer risk.
Observational studies suggest estrogen through the skin carries a lower clot risk than tablets.

myths.myth_en: HRT gives every woman breast cancer.
myths.fact_en: The risk depends on the type of therapy, the woman's age and how long it is used. For many women near menopause, the extra risk is small and the benefits are real. A doctor weighs this for each person.

myths.myth_en: HRT is only for hot flushes.
myths.fact_en: It also protects bone and treats vaginal and urinary symptoms.

myths.myth_en: Men don't need estrogen.
myths.fact_en: They do. Crashing estrogen in men harms bones, joints, libido and mood.

myths.myth_en: Estrogen makes women gain weight.
myths.fact_en: Weight changes around menopause are driven by age and falling estrogen, which moves fat to the belly. HRT has not been shown to cause weight gain.

entries.care_en: HRT replaces falling hormones around menopause, chosen for the person: the type, the route (tablet, patch or gel) and whether a progestogen is needed. It is reviewed regularly. Misuse looks different: men buying estrogen blockers online to 'control' estrogen during steroid use, or estrogen taken without the progestogen a woman with a uterus needs.
entries.abuse_en: Estrogen is natural, but the wrong hormone, in the wrong person, or with no follow-up, causes harm. Estrogen without a progestogen in a woman with a uterus raises the risk of uterine cancer. In men, pushing estrogen too high or too low both cause problems.
good_en: Relief of hot flushes, night sweats and sleep problems.
Protection against bone loss and fractures.
Relief of vaginal dryness and some urinary symptoms.
risks_en: Blood clots and stroke, higher with tablets and in older or higher-risk women, which is why doctors choose the route and check risk first.
Uterine cancer when estrogen is used without a progestogen in women with a uterus.
A small rise in breast cancer risk with some combined therapies used for many years.
In men, breast growth when levels run high, and bone and joint problems when levels are crushed.

entries.summary_en: The hormone that prepares and protects the uterus and supports pregnancy. In HRT it protects the uterine lining. Natural progesterone and synthetic progestins are different drugs.
does_en: Prepares the uterine lining after ovulation and keeps it stable.
Supports early pregnancy.
Balances estrogen's growth effect on the uterus.
Has a calming effect on the brain through a breakdown product, which can help sleep.
men_en: Men make small amounts in the adrenal glands and testes, mainly as a building block for other hormones.
It is rarely prescribed to men.
Some misused steroids (such as nandrolone and trenbolone) act on progesterone receptors, which is a misuse problem, not a natural one.
women_en: Levels rise after ovulation and fall before a period, if there is no pregnancy.
In pregnancy, the placenta makes large amounts.
Around menopause, women with a uterus who take estrogen need progesterone or a progestin to protect the uterine lining.
Low progesterone in the second half of the cycle can come with short cycles or spotting; a doctor looks for the cause.
trials_en: The large US hormone trial used a synthetic progestin, not body-identical progesterone.
Large observational studies suggest body-identical (micronized) progesterone may carry a lower breast cancer risk than some synthetic progestins. This has not been tested in large randomised trials.
Progesterone has been studied to prevent early birth in selected high-risk pregnancies, with results that depend on the group.

myths.myth_en: Progesterone and progestins are the same.
myths.fact_en: They are different molecules with different effects and risks. Many old HRT fears came from studies of one synthetic progestin.

myths.myth_en: Shop-bought progesterone creams are a safe form of HRT.
myths.fact_en: Over-the-counter creams vary a lot and have not been shown to protect the uterus. They are not a substitute for prescribed therapy.

entries.care_en: In HRT, a doctor adds progesterone to estrogen for women with a uterus and chooses the type and pattern. It is also used in fertility treatment and some pregnancies under specialist care. Misuse in this case is mostly self-treating with unregulated creams, or skipping the progestogen while using estrogen.
entries.abuse_en: Even a natural hormone can be used wrongly: an unproven cream used instead of real uterine protection, or hormones taken to 'balance' symptoms without tests to find the real cause.
good_en: Protects the uterine lining during estrogen therapy.
May improve sleep for some women.
Supports some pregnancies under specialist care.
risks_en: Drowsiness and dizziness, which is why it is often taken at night as advised by a doctor.
Uterine lining not protected when unregulated creams replace prescribed therapy.
Mood changes with some progestins.

entries.ar: دي إتش إي إيه · ديهيدرو إيبي أندروستيرون
entries.summary_en: An adrenal hormone the body turns into testosterone and estrogen. Levels peak in early adulthood and fall with age. Sold as a supplement in some countries but needs a prescription in many others. Anti-aging claims have not held up.
does_en: Acts as a building block for testosterone and estrogen.
Is a major source of androgens in women.
Circulates in a stored form (DHEA-S), the most abundant steroid in the blood.
men_en: In men, most testosterone comes from the testes, so DHEA adds little to testosterone in young men.
Part of it can turn into estrogen.
Trials in older men showed small or no effects on muscle, strength or wellbeing.
women_en: In women, DHEA is a major source of testosterone, so effects show more clearly.
Too much causes acne, oily skin and unwanted hair growth.
A vaginal form (prasterone) is approved in the US for painful sex after menopause.
In women whose adrenal glands do not work, some trials found small gains in wellbeing and libido.
trials_en: In older adults, trials of oral DHEA showed small, inconsistent effects on bone, muscle, mood and sexual function.
Vaginal DHEA improved painful sex after menopause in randomised trials, which led to approval.
It is studied in some fertility treatments, with uncertain results.

myths.myth_en: DHEA is a fountain of youth.
myths.fact_en: Levels fall with age, but replacing them did not reverse ageing in trials.

myths.myth_en: It is a natural supplement, so it is harmless.
myths.fact_en: It is a hormone that becomes testosterone and estrogen. It can cause hormone side effects and is banned in sport.

entries.care_en: Under a doctor, DHEA is used for specific problems, such as vaginal symptoms after menopause or adrenal failure, with follow-up of side effects. Misuse means taking it on your own as an anti-aging or muscle product.
entries.abuse_en: Because it converts into sex hormones, taking it without need can push testosterone or estrogen out of balance, especially in women. It is prohibited in sport under WADA's anabolic agents.
good_en: Relief of painful sex after menopause (vaginal form).
Possible wellbeing benefit for women with adrenal failure.
risks_en: Acne, oily skin and unwanted hair growth, mainly in women, when taken without need.
Hormone imbalance, which is why it should not be self-prescribed by people with hormone-sensitive conditions.
A positive sport doping test.
